title: APN_Construct Warehouse (CADSS/MAJAID), Trenton ON
description: Advance Procurement Notice Construct CADSS MAJAID Facility (Design Bid Build) Trenton, Ontario (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Trenton, ON. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Description of the Project and Services It is anticipated that the following 2-Step (Step 1: Request for Expression of Interest, Step 2: Tender Phase) solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN Number: TRS18081_73944 Approximate Estimate: $11M - $13M Anticipated Posting Step 1: Fall 2026 Anticipated Posting Step 2: Fall 2026 Description: Work of this contract comprises general contracting services and the supply and installation of all materials and labour required to construct a warehouse facility. The proposed facility will provide warehouse space for the Combat Aerial Delivery Support Section/Major Air Disaster (CADSS/MAJAID) Unit. The facility will support unit operations, including parachute inspection, drying, preparation, and packing activities; a dedicated carpentry shop; storage of operational material and equipment; and administrative office space. The facility will also accommodate material handling and warehouse operations, including the use of forklifts and other machinery within the building. The total estimated gross area of the project 1,554 m2. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a bidder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a bid for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential bidders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (TRS18081_73944); Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: Have submitted a response to the Step 1: RFEOI, have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Step 2: Tender Phase, meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the Step 2: Tender Phase, and Have submitted a tender to the Step 2: Tender Phase. DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors or Consultants that do not submit a tender or proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Steven Foster Team Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 613-813-4716 steven.foster@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the bidder or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: A.1. Application/Software Architect – Level 3
description: ISED is currently modernizing and maturing its end-to-end systems development lifecycle and project management lifecycle processes. The Application Software Architect – Level 3 will support the modernization, configuration, enhancement and ongoing evolution of the Clarity PPM platform throughout the two-year contract period. The resource will provide architecture, technical design, configuration, integration, analysis, documentation and technical advisory services in support of ISED's Clarity PPM environment. The resource will work under the direction of the Project Authority, who will establish priorities and assign work based on departmental requirements, the Clarity PPM roadmap and emerging business and technical needs. The resource will perform tasks including, but not limited to, the following: A. Architecture and Technical Design - Develop technical architectures, frameworks and strategies, either for an organization or for a major application area, to meet the business and application requirements. - Analyze functional requirements to identify information, procedures and decision flows. - Define input/output sources, including detailed plan for technical design phase, and obtain approval of the system proposal. - Advise on implementation paths, integration, interoperability and risk mitigation strategies relating to the implementation of Clarity PPM specific to the ISED Test and Production environments. B. Business Requirements Analysis - Elicit and analyze business requirements and related processes while adhering to relevant government policies and directives. C. Documentation and Standards - Evaluate existing procedures and methods, identify and document database content, structure, and application sub-systems, and develop data dictionary. - Define and document interfaces of manual to automated operations within application sub-systems, to external systems and between new and existing systems. - Identify and document system specific standards relating to programming, documentation and testing such as program libraries, data dictionaries, naming conventions. D. Clarity PPM Configuration and Advisory Services - Provide advice and hands-on services to architect and configure Clarity PPM in version 16.3x or more recent version. - Provide advice and hands-on expertise related to reporting requirements, including reporting to Treasury Board. - Provide advice and expertise on Government of Canada direction in Clarity PPM implementations. - Provide advice and expertise on private sector direction in Clarity PPM implementations.

title: Advance Procurement Notice - Independent Certifier for Alexandra Bridge Replacement Project
description: His Majesty the King in right of Canada, as represented by the Minister of Public Works and Government Services Canada and operating as Public Service Procurement Canada (“PSPC” or “Canada”), is contemplating a procurement process for the provision of Independent Certifier ("IC") services for the Alexandra Bridge Replacement Project (the “Project”). The purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice ("APN") is to provide interested parties with preliminary information regarding the requirement and the anticipated procurement process for the provision of IC services for the Project (the "Procurement Process"). This APN is also intended to promote early market awareness and engagement with organizations that possess the qualifications and experience required to deliver IC services for the Project. This APN is not part of the Procurement Process, and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by Canada to proceed with the Procurement Process. No agreement or contract will be entered into based on this APN. Canada reserves the right to amend, cancel, suspend, or modify the contemplated procurement strategy and requirements at any time.

title: RFP – Pilot Scale Multi-Mode Arc Furnace
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Description of Requirement: Natural Resources Canada requires a detailed engineering design and timeline for a pilot scale multi-mode arc furnace together with power supply and control systems, a continuous feeding system, a primary off-gas treatment system and ancillary equipment. The requirement includes the option for the Contractor to fabricate the furnace and deliver it to CanmetMATERIALS' Hamilton laboratory, with additional options for the purchase of spare parts and additional technical support. The delivery and completion of the detailed engineering design must be completed by March 1 2027, the period of the contract is from contract award to March 31 2028. If the option to produce the furnace is exercised, the furnace must be delivered, commissioned, and installed by March 1 2029, and the term of the contract will be extended to March 31 2031. Canada will hold an Offeror’s conference virtually on September 23 2026, beginning at 1:00 PM EDT. Participation in this conference is optional.

The selected consultant will provide the services identified in the Project Briefon a Task Authorization basis to support the delivery of the CHS Project during the Co-development Phase and will support the Crown by providing objective expertise in laboratory planning, building systems integration, design development oversight, and constructability review of the selected Development Partner’s Technical Submittals under the Development Phase Agreement (DPA) Works located in Gatineau. Late submissions will not be considered. Proposals may be submitted in either of Canada's official languages.

title: W8703-270059 - Medium Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) RFP
description: Offer submissions must be submitted by 27 October 2026 by 14:00 EDT. The Defence Investment Agency, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, is soliciting bids for the acquisition of a Medium Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) capability. The requirement supports defence and security operations through the provision of deployable medium-range UAS capabilities for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, situational awareness, force protection, training, experimentation, and other operational requirements. The procurement includes the supply and delivery of a minimum of forty (40) UAS Systems, associated payloads, ground control stations, support equipment, technical publications, spare parts, software and firmware support, and train-the-trainer services. The requirement also includes airworthiness support, cybersecurity assurance, supply chain security, spectrum supportability, configuration management, and lifecycle sustainment requirements. This procurement is limited to qualified suppliers holding a Stream 1 Supply Arrangement under the Defence Drone Initiative (DDI).

title: W8703-270072 Request For Proposal Domestic UAS Bulk Purchase RFP
description: Offer submissions must be submitted by 27 October 2026 by 14:00 EDT. The Defence Investment Agency, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, is soliciting bids for the acquisition of a Domestic General Purpose Uncrewed Aircraft System (GPUAS) capability. The requirement supports domestic operations conducted by the Canadian Army, including intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance activities, situational awareness, force protection, disaster response, search and rescue support, infrastructure assessment, training, and experimentation. The procurement includes the supply and delivery of a minimum of eighty (80) UAS systems, associated payloads, ground control stations, support equipment, technical publications, spare parts, software and firmware support, train-the-trainer services and includes airworthiness support, cybersecurity assurance, supply chain security, spectrum supportability, configuration management, and lifecycle sustainment requirements. This procurement is limited to qualified suppliers holding a Stream 1 Supply Arrangement under the Defence Drone Initiative (DDI).

title: Senior Leader Cutterhead Dredge Forum
description: On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Senior Leader Cutterhead Dredge Forum will provide a platform for collaboration focused on challenges and opportunities in the cutterhead dredging industry. This forum is open to all cutterhead dredging companies that are currently performing business in the New Orleans District or are interested in doing so. The dredge forum will provide an opportunity for dredging industry leaders to meet with USACE senior leaders and technical personnel to discuss New Orleans District dredging projects and funding. There will be two (2) attendee slots (leadership positions) available per company. If your company is interested in attending, please complete one registration form for each company and submit no later than October 16, 2026. Should an attendee/company have a question they would like to be discussed at the forum, please submit the inquiries via email to Yojna Calix at Yojna.Calix@usace.army.mil and Ashley Wainright at Ashley.Wainright@usace.army.mil, no later than 25 September 2026. Time: 9:00am - 12:00pm (CST) Location: USACE New Orleans District Headquarters District Assembly Room (DARM) 7400 Leake Avenue New Orleans, LA 70118 This event is free of charge. All attendees will be required to Pre-register for the event for attendance and to gain access to the installation. Each company should submit one registration with both attendees� information. Furthermore, information about the company's cutterhead dredges, as well as dredging experience in the last three years, will be a part of the registration submittal and must be completed. TO REGISTER: Please register at: https://form.jotform.com/251965714470159 The acquisition forecast information does not represent a pre-solicitation notice or a Request for Quotation/Proposal and is not a commitment by the Government to purchase products or services. We look forward to meeting with you.

title: F108--Radioactive Waste Removal and Disposal Services
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for Radioactive Waste Removal & Disposal Services as identified in the Statement of Work (SOW) for the Ann Arbor VA Medical Center in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The contractor shall furnish all necessary tools, parts, labor, supplies, materials, equipment, supervision and transportation necessary to furnish the services noted below. A DRAFT SOW is attached to this notice and is subject to change should a solicitation be issued as a result of this notice. Please respond if you have the ability and actual intention to complete this requirement. All of the following information is required in your response: SAM UEI NUMBER provide this in the email text GSA Contract Number provide this in the email text Capabilities Statement Confirmation of actual intent to submit an offer should an RFQ be posted in future Company name and address Point of contact information (name, phone, email) Socioeconomic size status (example: large business, small business, WOSB, SDVOSB, etc.) provide this in the email text This Sources Sought Notice is intended to locate any business capable of performance. The anticipated NAICS Code for this requirement is 562211. This is not a Request for Quotation and quotes shall not be reviewed at this time. The Government shall not be responsible for any costs incurred by the contractor because of this Sources Sought Notice. This notice shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to ultimately award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to any particular acquisition approach. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary; the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Responses shall be submitted to Jeanne Ortiz at jeanne.ortiz@va.gov by Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET). Responses MUST include 36C25027Q0045 in the subject line. PHONE CALLS SHALL NOT BE ACCEPTED FOR THIS NOTICE. DRAFT STATEMENT OF WORK Part I: General Information Introduction The Department of Veterans Affairs Ann Arbor Health Care System (VAAAHS) has a requirement for commercial radioactive waste removal for final disposition of liquid and solid uniform radioactive Low-Level Waste (LLW) to be completed by a qualified contractor in accordance with Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) regulations outlined in 10 CFR 20, 10 CFR 30, 10 CFR 40, 10 CFR 61 and 10 CFR 71 as well as all applicable United States Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations outlined in 49 CFR, and any applicable Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) regulations for required training, handling, packaging, labeling, placarding, transporting, and final disposition. Timely disposal of radioactive waste requires a vender with NRC licenses for treatment and disposal of radioactive and radioactive mixed hazardous waste (mixed waste). A successful bidder shall have Department of Transportation (DOT) registration for transportation of hazardous materials and personnel who are certified as being trained for handling, packaging, and shipping radioactive and mixed hazardous waste. Failure to manage radioactive waste including timely treatment and disposal could result in regulatory violations, fines, and/or the revocation of the VAAAHS permit to use radioactive material under the Department of Veterans Affairs Master Materials Licenses issued by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The VAAAHS system has two locations in which radioactive LLW will be picked up, 2215 Fuller Road, Ann Arbor, Michigan and 1200 South Detroit Avenue, Toledo, Ohio. Part II: Requirements Qualifications and Responsibilities of Contacted Personnel: A qualified contactor must have an active Radioactive Materials License granted by the NRC or an Agreement State to be able to handle, possess and dispose of the radioactive waste outlined in the next section. All transporters must maintain a current commercial driver s license (CDL) with a hazardous materials endorsement (H) to verify that the drivers possess the knowledge and skills necessary to handle and transport DOT class 7 radioactive materials. All applicable state and local permits must also be maintained by the contractor. All expenses associated with these qualifications are at the expense of the contractor and shall not be billed to the Federal Government. 2. Services to Be Performed: a. The contractor shall provide a current copy of their Radioactive Materials License as well as proof of transporter radiation safety training and CDLs. b. The contractor shall provide a template for both spent sealed sources and radioactive waste summary/inventory forms to be completed by the VAAAHS and submitted to the contractor prior to removal from the facility. There shall be no charge for this service. c. The contractor shall provide a current uniform low-level radioactive waste manifest (NRC Form 540 or equivalent substitute) that is to be filled out in its entirety and signed by both the contractor and the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff at the time of transfer of sealed sources and radioactive waste. There shall be no charge for this service. The waste manifest shall be compared against the sealed source and radioactive waste summary/inventory forms to ensure they match prior to transport away from the facility. Any discrepancies shall be resolved prior to transport. The contractor shall provide all required packaging such as boxes, pails, etc. for safe transportation of sealed sources and radioactive waste in accordance with NRC and DOT regulation. e. The Contractor shall take all necessary radioactive measurements and ensure that the packages are properly labeled in accordance with NRC and DOT regulations prior to transport. f. The contractor shall coordinate radioactive waste pick-up services with the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff. g. The Contractor shall remove the radioactive waste no less than once per contract year and not to exceed two pickups during the contract period: Any patient treatment waste byproduct material with Atomic Numbers 1-83, 88, and 89 in any form that includes unused radioactive unit dose vials (aqueous liquid) or patient radioactive waste (Biological/Sharps) not to exceed 50 pounds. Any byproduct material with Atomic Numbers 3-83 radioactive sealed sources or radioactive waste not to exceed 200 pounds. This includes sealed sources at locations of use and or unsealed radioactive waste generated. Scintillation Vials Liquid scintillation cocktail in vials containing byproduct material with Atomic Numbers 1-83, 88, and 89. Liquid Mixed Waste Radioactive waste containing EPA characteristic and/or listed hazardous material. This waste stream will be packaged in shipping containers according to waste profile requirements specified by the successful bidder. In accordance with 10 CFR Part 20 (Appendix G) a written notification that the contractor has received the radioactive shipments that were picked up from the VAAAHS must be provided to the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff. The NRC Form 540 or equivalent substitute must also be returned with item number 9 filled out with the contractor s signature acknowledging confirmation of the receipt of the radioactive waste. A final disposal certificate shall also be provided to the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff when final processing has been completed. The contractor shall be responsible for any leaks or spills that occur after taking possession of radioactive waste and spent sealed sources. Part III: Supporting Information Response Time Contractor shall respond by email within one week of when services are requested by email via the Ann Arbor VA Medical Center Radiation Safety Staff to schedule service with the Ann Arbor VA Medical Center Radiation Safety Staff. Contractor shall be on-site for service within three hours of the scheduled date/time unless there are unforeseeable circumstances that require rescheduling

title: 3PL Follow-on Effort RFI
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Federal Acquisition Service (FAS), General Supplies and Services (GSS) Portfolio, Office of Supply Chain Management (SCM) and Internal and Emergency Acquisition Division (IEAD) has a requirement a Third Party Logistics (3PL) provider in support of export operations to support overseas customers. Historically, these customers had previously been serviced by GSA and Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) distribution centers.This effort includes receipt of inbound Transatlantic and Transpacific ocean shipments from multiple award schedule vendors, inspection and preparation for shipment of goods or containers to an intermediate destination, then to another destination, i.e. transshipment; as well as shipment consolidation, ensuring readiness for onward movement in accordance with required Department of Defense (DoD) and Federal regulations through small package carriers, the U.S. Postal System (USPS) and Defense Transportation System (DTS), and reporting on noted discrepancies. Requirement synopsis: This requirement is Export Operations Support through the use of a Third-Party Logistics (3PL) to better align GSA warehousing, cargo movement and distribution processes with industry standards and simplify disposal, hazardous movement, storage and distribution requirements. See Google link in RFI attachment for detailed questions.

title: Kompostitarkastusten hyvien käytäntöjen kehittämishankkeen hankinta
description: Kompostitarkastusten hyvien käytäntöjen kehittämishankkeen hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on Hankintayksikön Kompostitarkastusten hyvien käytäntöjen kehittämishankkeen hankinta. Tarkemmin hankinnan kohteena on asiantuntijapalvelu, jossa tehtävänä on laatia selvitys kompostitarkastusten nykytilasta sekä opas ja viestintämateriaalia kompostitarkastusten hyvistä käytännöistä. Hanke on tarkoitus toteuttaa yhteistyössä Suomen Kuntaliitto ry:n, kuntien jätehuoltoviranomaisten sekä tarvittavien muiden viranomaisten ja asiantuntijatahojen kanssa. Hankkeessa tulee lisäksi kuulla kotikompostointia harjoittavia asukkaita tarkoituksenmukaisella tavalla. Tiedonkeruussa voidaan hyödyntää esimerkiksi kyselyitä, haastatteluja ja työpajoja. Palveluntuottaja vastaa hankkeen suunnittelusta, toteutuksesta, sidosryhmäyhteistyöstä, aineiston analysoinnista, raportoinnista sekä hankkeessa tuotettavan oppaan ja muun viestintämateriaalin laatimisesta ja hankkeen tulosten esittelystä yleisö- ja sidosryhmätilaisuuksissa. Materiaali tuotetaan pääasiassa suomenkielisenä, mutta opas laaditaan myös ruotsiksi ja yleistajuinen viestintämateriaali myös ruotsiksi ja englanniksi. Ympäristöministeriö vastaa oppaan julkaisemisesta Ympäristöministeriön julkaisuja -sarjassa. Hankinnan kohteena oleva työ alkaa mahdollisimman pian hankintasopimuksen solmimisen jälkeen ja päättyy viimeistään 30.4.2027. Suomenkielisen oppaan ja viestintämateriaalien tulee olla valmiina viimeistään 31.3.2027. Valtakunnallinen info- tai verkkotilaisuus tulee toteuttaa viimeistään viikolla 14. Muiden tuotosten tulee olla valmiina tai toteutettuna viimeistään 30.4.2027. Tarjouksessa tulee esittää palvelun toteutuksesta vastaava asiantuntija (projektipäällikkö). Projektipäälliköllä tulee olla tukenaan palvelun toteutuksessa riittävä määrä muita asiantuntijoita. Hankintayksikkö on varannut toimeksiannon toteuttamiseen enintään 65 000 euroa (+mahdollinen alv). Hankinnan tarkempi kuvaus on liitteessä 1 (Palvelun kuvaus). Liitteessä 2 (CV-lomake) ilmoitetut hankinnan kohdetta koskevat vaatimukset ovat pakollisia vaatimuksia. Tarjottavan palvelun tulee täyttää kaikki palvelulle asetetut pakolliset vaatimukset, jotta sen voidaan katsoa olevan tarjouspyynnön mukainen. Hankintayksikkö valitsee yhden (1) toimittajan, jonka kanssa se tekee sopimuksen.,

title: Airfield Blast Shield
description: Amendment 0001 (13 Oct 2026): The purpose of this amendment is to � Extend the Proposal Due Date to 27 October 2026. � All other solicitation requirements remain unchanged and in full effect. 1.1 PROJECT DESCRIPTION: 1.1.1 Work under this project shall consist of providing all plant, labor, equipment, appliances, materials, and performing all operations required to cover the fabrication and erection of new Blast Deflector Fences for the B1-B. All work shall comply with the contract specifications and shall be in accordance with the latest International Building Code (IBC), National Fire Codes, Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC), Engineering Technical Letters (ETL�s), and all applicable Federal, State and local regulations/codes. 2.1 GENERAL: 2.1.1 The blast deflector shall be of the curved, non-perforated, galvanized, corrugated type, with corrugations running in a horizontal direction. The Lynnco Type GS-20-2 as manufactured by Blast Deflectors, Inc shall be considered as the standard for this work. At the option of the Contracting Officer, alternate types of blast deflectors may be considered provided the drawings and specifications of alternate types are approved by Contracting Officer. The blast fence shall be furnished and installed by a manufacturer/contractor with blast fence experience. The blast fence shall be capable of withstanding the afterburner throttle at 30,000 lbs thrust of a B1-B Bomber engine nozzle 90 ft/ (min.) from front of deflector foundation. Extrapolated temperature is approx. 1400 ? velocity @ 900 MPH. 2.1.2 Haul Route: Approved haul route is from the Tye Gate, Third Street, Ave E, Second Street, to Flightline. Haul Route subject to change based on Flightline Restrictions. Contractors are required to use the Tye Gate for all access. 2.1.3 Construction Storage Yard & Contractor Limits: Contractor shall store all equipment and material within the designed laydown yard. Contractors shall restore this area to pre-construction conditions. Regardless of the area, the yard shall be fenced. Contractor shall keep the fence well maintained and the site clean and mowed. Contractor shall obtain approval for any project limits changes prior to construction commencement from 7 CES through the Contracting Officer. The approved laydown yard will be provided at the pre-construction meeting. 2.1.4 Contractor shall provide material submittals for all materials & products used in the project on an AF Form 3000. All PDFs shall be from original electronic documents; no scans allowed due to file size. 2.1.5 Work is located in a restricted area. The contractor shall submit a two-week schedule to the Escort POC at least one week prior to work starting to ensure escorts are assigned. The schedule should include start/end times for each day, crew sizes, and work locations. 3.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR CONTRUCTION: 3.1.1 Structural frames which support the deflecting surface will be of structural shapes, rolled, punches, and prefabricated for bolting together at site. Deflecting surface will be of galvanized corrugated steel with a minimum of 2 oz. zinc coating per Fed. Spec. WW-P-00405. Sheets shall have a section modulus of not less than 0.0163 inches curbed per inch and shall be of corrosion resistant material with yield point in 50,000 psi range. 3.1.2 All bolts subject to blast temperatures shall be of SAE 1038 steel, heat treated. All nuts, except on anchor bolts, shall be made of all-steel, self-locking type. 4.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR ANCHORAGE 4.1.1 Blast Deflectors shall be installed on existing concrete. Existing concrete has a minimum thickness of 16�. Lynnco "Epoxy-Locked" anchors, with Lynnco No. 22 Epoxy Resin were used to lock in place the existing blast deflectors. 5.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR ASSEMBLY: 5.1.1 All components will be assembled by bolting together with flat washers, under heads and nuts. Welding, brazing or burning of holes is not permitted. All nuts and bolts will be tightened to torques specified by manufacturer. 6.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR FINISH: 6.1.1 All bolts, nuts and washers will be cadmium or zinc plated. All structural members, parts, and corrugated metal will be hot dip galvanized with a minimum coating of 2.0 oz. zinc per square foot of surface. Painting of galvanized surfaces is not required, but any galvanized surface badly scratched or marred, will be re-galvanized or otherwise repaired to the satisfaction of the Contracting Officer. 6.1.2 Contractor shall paint the corresponding aircraft parking position number on the front of the blast deflectors. The Contactor shall provide a 2�x2� number sign mounted 15� above the concrete at the midpoint on the backside of the blast deflector. Markings/sign shall follow details 2 and 8 on sheet C2 of the attached drawings. 7.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR ALTERNATIVES: 7.1.1 At the option of the Contracting Officer, and as specified in Paragraph 2, the Contractor may substitute an alternate type of blast deflector, providing that the following information and data is submitted, prior to the time of bid opening and approved in writing. 7.1.2 Contractor will submit for approval a tabulation of results of full-scale instrumented field tests witnessed and certified by an accredited testing laboratory, in which proposed alternate is subject to the intermediate throttle power of similar engines totaling # 30,000 afterburner thrust @ approx. 90 feet distance from the leading edge of the deflector measured along centerline of bast impingement. Tabulation must show the maximum pressure in psi, temperature in degrees F., vibration frequency in CPS, and vibration amplitude in inches, taken at the centerline of blast impingement on deflector. The results of all such readings may not be greater than the readings submitted for the specified deflector, for each corresponding item. 7.1.3 Contractor must submit results of smoke-pot tests behind similar deflectors, demonstrating that smoke and gases are deflected in a vertical direction, with no evidence of smoke dispersal behind deflectors. 7.1.4 Contractor must submit evidence of satisfactory operation for at least two (2) years in actual field service for continued testing of similar aircraft and jet engines. 7.1.5 Contractor must submit detailed design analysis, showing loads and stresses in structural members, deflecting surface and bolted joints, using the maximum pressure measured in Paragraph 7.1.2, as the average pressure for load calculations. Welds subjected to tension or vibration may not be used; all bolts must be heat treated if subjected to blast temperatures. 7.1.6 Because of thermal shock and cavitation effects, which results in cracking and spalling, concrete deflectors may not be used as an alternate. Perforated deflecting surfaces are not acceptable for this use.

INVITATION FOR BID W9126G26BA010 for Joe Pool Dam Slide Repair at Joe Pool Lake, Texas. This announcement is a competitive small business set aside, firm-fixed price, Joe Pool Dam Slide Repair civil works construction services at Joe Pool Lake, Texas. The North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990-Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction which has a small business size standard of $45 Million. The Product Service Code is Z2PC-Repair or Alteration of Dams. Project Scope: The contractor shall repair four shallow slides (Slides 18, 20, 21, and 28) on the upstream and downstream dam embankment slopes. Work includes the removal of slide debris; excavation of the slide area with bench-cutting into the stable embankment and a keyway into the foundation toe; lime-treatment of excavated soil; placement and compaction of treated soil to restore original design contours; and final surface restoration with riprap on the upstream slope and topsoil with vegetation on the downstream slope.

description: Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to replace the existing docks and marine fueling system at the Sidney Operations Centre (SOC), located at 2220 Harbour Road in Sidney, British Columbia, which serves as the primary Parks Canada Agency office and marine operations base for the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. The work includes the removal, disposal, and replacement of the existing docks, pilings, and associated servicing systems. The Contractor will supply and install new aluminum-frame docks, pilings, water and electrical services, dock lighting, and a new fueling system consisting of a 5,000-litre fuel tank, fuel lines, and dispenser. All in-water works, including the removal of the existing docks and pilings and the installation of the new docks, must be completed within the lower-risk fisheries window between December 1, 2026, and February 15, 2027. Work occurring above the high-water line may be completed outside of this period. The Contractor will be required to implement the mitigation measures identified in Parks Canada Agency’s Basic Impact Assessment to minimize environmental risks and impacts associated with the project. TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

title: Ireland – Recreational, cultural and sporting services – Dublin City Council Contract for Architect Led Integrated Design Team for the Installation of a Pontoon at Islandbridge
description: The stretch of the River Liffey near Islandbridge, is home to over 13 Rowing Clubs – one of which belongs to Dublin City Council. In order to link the eastern length of the Liffey from Islandbridge, the Community, Culture and Local Area Services Department of Dublin City Council has obtained planning permission for an access walkway and pontoon to be constructed on one of the small islands east of the weir. This will allow rowers starting at Islandbridge to have access down to Ringsend and vice versa safely. The project comprises a pontoon with associated walkways to facilitate access to the river for rowing boats and kayaks. The project will provide for a platform that would minimize damage to bankside vegetation when launching and retrieving boats and allow a safe platform for kayakers and boaters to embark and disembark. The Islandbridge location has extensive heritage and ecology. In keeping with this, minimal deviation from the existing design and methodology is required to comply with planning regulations. The works proposed plan to combine the following elements: a) A floating pontoon system within the River Liffey anchored to the existing island shore. b) A new stone and concrete platform built out from the riverbank and connected to the pontoon by a new gangway. c) The removal of vegetation on approach to the pontoon and installation of a new access walkway from the south upper River Liffey at the weir to the new pontoon located north on the lower River Liffey. d) The temporary removal, refurbishment and reinstatement of an existing steel footbridge located on the island. e) The removal of poor existing vegetation, pruning of existing healthy trees and the replanting of 25 new high-quality trees and growing shrubs all native to Ireland. f) Temporary regrading of land during site works for access onto the island. . Please note that this project is subject to funding. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID xxxxxxx – Input when notice created.

title: France – Software package and information systems – FOURNITURE D’UNE SOLUTION DE FEEDBACK MANAGEMENT (ENQUETES DE SATISFACTION CLIENTS & NPS) ET PRESTATIONS ASSOCIEES
description: . Les directions des branches Services-Courrier-Colis (BSCC) et Grand Public et Numérique (BGPN) de La Poste, représentant six volets fonctionnels, souhaitent renouveler leur solution de Feedback Management et d'Écoute Client. L'objectif est de se doter d’une solution en mode SaaS pour l'administration et la gestion des enquêtes de satisfaction : - création de l'enquête, - programmation, - routage ... - jusque l'exploitation du verbatim, - la restitution des avis et résultats - et en dernier lieu la possibilité de donner une réponse personnalisée au destinataire de l’enquête. . La solution devra permettre la restitution des résultats à tous les maillons de l'organisation (Siège et Territoires), via une connexion SSO, avec des profils et rôles d’utilisateurs différents. . La solution devra permettre la création de dashboard en autonomie selon le type de profil. Les flux de données proviennent de plusieurs SI internes et externes à La Poste, selon les typologies d'enquêtes. . La solution SaaS devra donc s'interfacer avec d'autres outils de La Poste. Les enquêtes couvrent des prestations de services variées au sein de La Poste pour l'ensemble des Directions citées. Chaque Direction a des besoins spécifiques. . La solution devra se conformer au Règlement Général sur la Protection des Données (RGPD). . Le traitement des données personnelles de La Poste, y compris l’hébergement, la sauvegarde et/ou la consultation devra impérativement être localisé au sein de l'Union Européenne (UE), d’un pays de l’Espace Economique Européen (EEE), d’un pays reconnu comme adéquat par l’Union Européenne.. La solution devra également respecter la Politique de Sécurité des SI du Groupe La Poste (PSSIG).

This procurement is to obtain High-Performance Computing (HPC) software development and technical support services for the GFDL. title: Renovate Building 736 Fort Leonard Wood, MO
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District (USACE) is seeking contractors to renovate Building 736 at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. Building 736 is a 40,640 Square Foot (SF), three story, permanent construction barrack facility was built in the 1960s and currently houses basic training/one station unit training (BT/OSUT) trainees. A design was completed by the Kansas City District Corps of Engineers in April 2019 and updated in accordance with UFC changes in June of 2024. This requirement will consist of selective demolition and renovation and modernization of one barracks building and associated sitework at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. This project includes renovation of a 40,640 SF Barracks Building and construction of an addition of approximately 3,000 SF addition to the building, and associate fine grading, landscaping, and other site work per the plans and specifications provided.

title: PTAG RFI: USPTO seeks Contractor to fabricate awards; certificates and medallions
description: ***10-14-2026 AMENDED*** 1) Answered all questions received by deadline. 2) For Answers, Please see attached PDF titled "RFI-27-1001_Awards-Certs-Medallions QA FINAL" ***10-6-2026 AMENDED*** 1) Revised deadline for questions to Friday, October 9, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET 2) Revised deadline for Responses to Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET 3) Revised attached PDF with new deadlines and to reflect that RFI-27-1001 is the correct identifier. The corrected attachment is titled "PTAG_ RFI-27-1001_ For awards certificates medallions_FINAL.V2" 4) Added attachment titled "PTAG_ RFI-27-1001_photos of career awards" THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 339999 - All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing and PSC 7690 - Miscellaneous Printed Matter Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) USPTO is seeking a contractor who can fulfill the agency�s requirements for the following awards, certificates, medallions, as well as appropriate packaging and direct shipping for each. This requirement includes manufacturing, assembly and preparing the awards for delivery and shipping directly to the recipient or to an agency office as required. The Office of Human Resource (OHR) supports a variety of non-monetary awards to recognize and reward employee excellence. Superior performance is generally considered as the type of employee performance that contributes, directly or indirectly, to the mission of the USPTO. These non-monetary awards include Bronze Medal Awards, Career Achievement Awards which includes Distinguished Career Awards and Exceptional Career Awards, Retirement Certificates, Directors Award, Length of Service Award and Leadership in Action Award. These awards range in style and type to include framed certificates, medals encased in leucite and presented with a certificate and display box and laser etched clear crystal desktop awards. Note: Sample photos of the awards are attached in a pdf to this RFI 1) Bronze Medal Awards- This award is used to recognize an organization, group or individual employees who have made a major impact on the effectiveness of the USPTO. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity per year is up to 450. 2) Distinguished Career Awards: This award marks at least 20 years of superior performance as an employee of the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 150. 3) Exceptional Career Awards: This award marks at least ten (10) years of superior performance with the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 275. 4) Retirement Certificates: The purpose of this certificate is to recognize USPTO employees upon the occasion of their retirement. These are ordered/requested upon notification of an employee retiring. Framed certificates are created throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 120. 5) Directors Award: The purpose of this award is to recognize individuals and/or group recognition for contributions to the Agency, Managers, supervisors or other employees may nominate those whose contributions have far exceeded expectations or reflect positively on the USPTO. These awards are sporadic throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 100. 6) Leadership in Action Award. The recipients are recognized during the USPTO Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony. The Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity of Leadership in Action awards is up to 400 per year. The three (3) award tiers are Supervisor of the Year (SOTY), Supervisor of the Year (SOTY) Finalist, Approved Nominated Supervisors. Each award tier has a different associated cost and quantity. 7) Length of Service Award: The purpose of this award is to recognized USPTO employee�s length of Federal service. This award is issued monthly. The estimated quantity per year is approximately 2,600. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of awards and services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE All interested contractors should provide the following information in their response via e-mail to the contacts listed below: The email subject should include: �RFI-27-1001 Awards fabrication sources sought� Your contractor name, address, SAM UEI, point of contact information, email, phone, website address. Your FSS Schedule contract number (Only if applicable). Any relevant certifications or other relevant authorizations Information about your firm�s ability to meet the requirements stated above Please provide a tailored capability statement addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. Please provide photos and specs of awards your company manufactures consistent with the requirements listed above. A link to award photos on your website will suffice as well. Past Performance � Please provide info on previous government agencies or private businesses you�ve done similar work for in the past. Please include a short description of the work done and photos of the awards provided (if possible) Please include civilian customer/Government Agency contact information including: contact name and organization, telephone number, and email address. QUESTIONS Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than Friday, October 9, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via email to roy.pitman@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE DEADLINE: Responses are due no later than Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via email to roy.pitman@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE Late responses may be considered at the government�s discretion. Disclaimer: This PTAG Sources Sought Request For Information (RFI) notice is issued solely for Market Research information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled in accordance with procurement integrity requirements. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

title: Microelectronics Sourcing Capability for Tobyhanna Army Depot (RFI 2)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to identify qualified Original Component Manufacturers (OCMs) and their Tier-1 direct distributors (directly working with manufacturer) capable of supplying commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS), industrial, and defense-grade microelectronics in sustained, large-scale production volumes for Circuit Card Assembly (CCA) integration. The primary objective is to transition from spot-market, broker-dependent, and decentralized procurement models toward resilient, long-term, direct-tier relationships with primary component fabricators and direct suppliers. The Government seeks insights into volume production capacity, minimum lead times, wafer/die allocations, packaging assurances, and transparent chain-of-custody protocols. Disclaimer: This RFI is published solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. See Attachment 1 - Request for Information for a full description of the Government's requirement for High-Volume Microelectronics Sourcing: Direct Manufacturer & Tier-1 Production Supply Chains.

title: USCIS FY27 1st Quarter Engagement with Industry
description: United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), Office of Contracting (OCON), will host its Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 First Quarter Engagement with Industry on October 27, 2026, beginning at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time. These quarterly engagements provide an opportunity for open dialogue between USCIS and industry regarding current and anticipated procurement requirements. The purpose of this event is to share the most current procurement-related information available for USCIS requirements. To participate as an attendee, please self-register using the Microsoft Teams link below: Microsoft Teams meeting https://events.gcc.teams.microsoft.com/event/74f50b56-1413-4370-8199-58b2c86f4a98@5e41ee74-0d2d-4a72-8975-998ce83205eb?source=copyLinkLegacyShareLinkDialog USCIS uses Microsoft Teams to conduct these industry engagements. Attendees will be muted upon entry, and attendee video will be disabled. Only presenters will be on video. USCIS plans to record this event and post the recording on its YouTube channel after the event. Once available, the recording link will be posted as an update to this SAM.gov announcement. USCIS expects to post draft presentation slides to this announcement on or about October 13, 2026. Format and Questions The event will be organized by execution division and then by the Associate Chief portfolio supporting each program office. Presenters will brief the requirements within each portfolio, including new information and updates, as applicable. Following each portfolio briefing, USCIS will address questions related to that portfolio. Attendees may submit questions through the Microsoft Teams Q&A feature or ask questions verbally when the floor is opened for questions. Please include the requirement title and the applicable slide number and/or Acquisition Planning Forecast System (APFS) number, if available. To help USCIS manage the agenda and stay on schedule, USCIS will address only questions related to the portfolio currently being presented. Once USCIS moves to the next portfolio, it will not return to take additional live questions on a prior portfolio. USCIS strongly encourages industry to submit questions in advance. Advance submission allows USCIS to coordinate with the appropriate program and contracting personnel and provide the most accurate and timely information available during the event. Please submit advance questions to USCIS_Vendoroutreach@uscis.dhs.gov no later than 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 20, 2026. USCIS will collect and review questions received during the event. USCIS will post responses to those questions as an update to this announcement. Information posted to SAM.gov after the event will supersede information provided during the live engagement. Disclaimer The information provided during this event and in the accompanying presentation is for planning purposes only. It does not constitute a pre-solicitation notice, invitation for bids, request for proposals, or request for quotations. The Government is under no obligation to purchase products or services discussed unless and until a formal solicitation or invitation for bids is issued and a contract or order is awarded. All planned procurements are subject to change or cancellation. Requirements currently under an active solicitation or source selection will not be further discussed. Questions regarding those requirements should be directed to the designated Contracting Officer. The remaining Fiscal Year 2027 quarterly industry engagement schedule is provided below: 2nd Quarter: January 26, 2027 3rd Quarter: April 27, 2027 4th Quarter: July 27, 2027

description: Sources Sought: Firm-Fixed-Price, Non-Personal Healthcare Services � EMT Paramedic & EMT Basics Services at the Cheyenne River Health Center, Eagle Butte, South Dakota. Sources Sought Notice Number: IHS1528529 This Sources Sought Notice is for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation, an obligation or commitment by the Indian Health Service. This notice is intended for market research to determine the availability of Indian Small Businesses Economic Enterprise (ISBEE), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE), 8(a) Business Development programs, HUBZone (Historically Underutilized Business Zone), WOSB (Women-Owned Small Business), SDVOSB (Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business) and other responsible sources. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The anticipated applicable NAICS code for this acquisition is 561320, Temporary Help Services - other relevant NAICS codes will be considered based on responses received. BACKGROUND The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area (GPA), Cheyenne River Health Center, plans to identify potential sources providing Non-Personal Service Contract for EMT services in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS). 2.0 OBJECTIVE The objective of the Cheyenne River Health Center is to raise the physical, mental, social and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. To complete this mission, the Cheyenne River Health Center requires contractor support to provide for EMT services. SCOPE The contractor shall furnish EMT services according to the Performance Work Statement (PWS). These services will be compatible with the facility�s operating capacity and equipment. CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS/ AND PERSONNEL QUALIFICATIONS Refer to the Performance Work Statement (PWS). TYPE OF ORDER This is a sources sought notice for a firm-fixed-price contract. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE Period of Performance: Base Year with four (4), one (1) year option periods. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE Cheyenne River Health Center 24276 166th Street Eagle Butte, South Dakota 57625 Tour of Duty: Refer to the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor shall ensure the contractually required support level is maintained at all times. This contract is for specified skill types/levels - not for specific individuals. The Contractor shall ensure that all Contractor Personnel are present for all hours of the workday. If for any reason the specified staffing levels are not maintained, due to vacation, leave, appointments, etc. and replacement Personnel will not be provided, the Contractor shall obtain the written approval of the Supervisor/ designee or the COR II prior to the Contractor Personnel's absence. Otherwise, the Contractor shall provide a fully qualified replacement so there is no gap in service. The Contractor Personnel shall be available for work in the work area per work direction schedule. The Contractor shall ensure Contractor Personnel provide professional effort and conform to Government policies regarding daily lunch breaks and other breaks. The Contractor shall ensure Contractor Personnel communicate to the Supervisor for reporting to work as it relates to inclement weather (late due to travel conditions etc.). If a Contractor Personnel is absent due to illness for three or more consecutive days, the Contractor shall provide to the COR II written documentation from a qualified health care provider that Contractor Personnel is free from communicable disease and state the cause of the Contractor Personnel's illness. Statement that Contractor Personnel is fit for service may be requested if deemed necessary. If services are not provided by Contractor Personnel, the CRHC reserves the right to procure such services from another source and deduct these costs and all administrative costs from payments due the Contractor. PAYMENT INVOICE SUBMISSION AND PAYMENT In compliance with the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) M-15-19 memorandum Improving Government Efficiency and Saving Taxpayer Dollars Through Electronic Invoicing directing Federal agencies to adopt electronic invoicing as the primary means to disburse payment to vendors. Invoices submitted under any award resulting from this solicitation will be required to utilize the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) in accordance with HHSAR 352.232-71, Electronic Submission and Processing of Payment Requests. IPP is a secure, web-based electronic invoicing system provided by the U.S. Department of the Treasury�s Bureau of the Fiscal Service, in partnership with the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRSTL). Respondents to this solicitation are encouraged to register an account with IPP if they have not already done so. If your organization is already registered to use IPP, you will not be required to re-register, however, we encourage you to make sure your organization and designated IPP user accounts are valid and up to date. The IPP website address is: https://www.ipp.gov. If you require assistance registering or IPP account access, please contact the IPP Helpdesk at (866) 973-3131 (M-F 8AM to 6PM ET), or IPPCustomerSupport@fiscal.treasury.gov. Failure to do so will be at your firm�s own risk. The following information shall be included in the capability statement: Company name, address, email address, website address, telephone number, and business size (i.e., small business, 8(a), woman owned, veteran owned, etc.) and type of ownership for the organization. Company Point of Contact�s Name, telephone number, and e-mail address. Company POC shall have the authority and knowledge to clarify responses. System for Award Management (SAM) Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, expiration, and registration status. All respondents must register on the SAM located at http://www.sam.gov . Applicable company GSA Schedule number or other available procurement vehicle. Capability Statement: Detailed capability statement addressing the company�s qualifications and ability to provide the requirements listed in the Performance Work Statement, with appropriate and specific documentation supporting claims of recent organizational and staff capability to support this requirement. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. Experience: Provide a list of 3-5 private industry or Government contracts for the same services that you have performed within the last 3 years. For each contract, include the company�s Point of Contact�s name, email address, telephone number, dollar value of contract, and description of the services provided on the contract. The Government may contact these entities to conduct past performance checks. Reference letters accepted. Staffing Levels: Provide evidence your company has adequate levels of qualified healthcare provider staff to meet the Qualifications and Requirements listed in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Staffing Capability: Provide the last time you successfully placed a provider in a contract position. Provide detailed information such as name, email address, telephone number, dollar value of contract, and description of the services provided on the contract. Technical Capability: Provide a response to how the company will respond to staff shortages / absenteeism / replacement in providing services. title: LOC Novel High-Density Optical Data Storage
description: The Library of Congress, hereinafter referred to as the �Library� or �LOC�,� is exploring innovative preservation methods for its digital collections. The LOC is seeking to determine the feasibility of utilizing ultra-high density optical data storage designed for the long-term preservation of a subset of the Library�s digital collections. Currently, the Library manages over 1 billion unique objects of digital preservation data (~33 petabytes) via traditional storage methods. For longevity and reduced migration intervals, it may be reasonable for this portion of data to be permanently stored on a novel medium. The focus would be on a solution that exhibits high areal density, a long lifespan, reduced maintenance/migration cycles, is immutable, and displays a high level of durability. The Library aims to demonstrate the feasibility of an innovative optical data storage solution as a high-density, scalable, and durable medium for storing its preservation collection. The Library wishes to examine the feasibility of this method on a small subset of its digital collections. To be successful, a variety of data formats�including video, audio, text, and images� must be encoded onto the media, errors must be detected/recorded, preservation techniques must be validated and select data must be recalled/read with high fidelity. This work will contribute to the boundary pushing field of high-density optical data storage while pushing the boundaries of access and preservation. The desired outcomes of this requirement are as follows: The successful writing of 1TB of the Library�s digital data in various formats (video, audio, images, text) onto a robust high-density optical media designed to outlast legacy storage solutions at a higher areal density. The determination of the accuracy of the writing process by demonstrating early-stage error detection and ultimate 100% recovery of data. The documentation of successful processes, shortcomings, error rates, timelines, potential solutions to issues, risks, trends, and technological improvements throughout the period of performance as they pertain to the media of choice. Proof of concept for the potential indefinite storage approach of the Library�s data on a novel optical storage medium. The successful recall and reading of all Library-furnished digital files that have been encoded on the media of choice. The isolation of a subset of the data will be carefully curated and stored for the purposes of an educational and artistic display. This will used for educational and display purposes for Library visitors.

title: Architect & Engineering Services, Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award (A&E) Contracts needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs required by Federal Prison Industries (FPI)
description: The Federal Prison Industries (FPI) intends to solicit and award a competitively negotiated Architect and Engineer (A&E) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Contract needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs. The Architect and Engineer (A&E) shall furnish professional architectural, engineering, and related technical services, as specified herein, to the United States Government, Department of Justice, Federal Prison Industries (FPI). The resulting contracts will consist of a one?year base period and will include options for four additional one?year periods. All work performed under this contract shall pertain to projects located at FPI facilities within the contiguous United States. Pursuant to the terms of this contract, the A&E may be required to perform services under the following major categories, including other closely related services as necessary: � Review design and construction documents prepared by other A&E firms or by FPI personnel. � Prepare, develop, and produce design and construction documents for new facility construction, facility additions, and renovation or modernization of existing facilities. � Develop detailed and accurate cost estimates for construction activities, renovations, contract modifications, and claims. � Conduct Value Engineering (V/E) analyses and perform additional cost evaluation studies, as required. � Develop, maintain, and update project schedules and construction schedules. � Provide assistance in preventing, mitigating, and resolving disputes or claims arising from design or construction activities. � Furnish comprehensive architectural and engineering services encompassing all disciplines necessary to ensure the successful execution and completion of assigned projects. � Provide, as required, studies; design development; construction documents; technical specifications; support during bid negotiation; construction administration; and project closeout services. � Develop procedures, prepare construction documents and work statements, support master planning efforts, conduct regulatory compliance evaluations, and assist in the preparation of design?build documentation. � Prepare construction specifications that uphold the principles of full and open competition. � Comply with all general requirements applicable to task orders issued under this contract. In accordance with the Brooks Architect-Engineer Act, award(s) shall be made to the successful firm(s) based on demonstrated competence and qualifications to perform the services at fair and reasonable prices. Prior to this solicitation issuance, technical evaluations were conducted. This solicitation was then issued to the most highly rated firm(s). Therefore, in response to the solicitation, consideration for a contract award will be based solely upon the hourly rates, overhead and profit that are proposed and found to be fair and reasonable. Offerors are advised that award maybe made without discussions. Therefore, the initial proposal should provide sufficient information to recommend award without discussions and should reflect the offeror�s ability to perform at a reasonable price.

title: Solicitation - Residential Reentry Services and Home Confinement Services within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island.
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000009 Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services and Home Confinement (HC) services for male and female offenders located within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island. Home Confinement radius is within 100 miles of the RRC facility. The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which are located within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island. Home Confinement radius is within 100 miles of the RRC facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four one-year options periods. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 8 beds (8 males and 0 females) and an estimated maximum 20 beds facility in which 18 beds will be designated for males and 2 beds designated for females. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 3 placements and an estimated maximum 8 placements to include both male and female. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000009 will be available on or about August 28, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. description: Project Title/Location: DESIGN-BID-BUILD P084 NEXT GENERATION TORPEDO INTEGRATION LAB, NAVAL STATION NEWPORT, NEWPORT RI SOLICITATION NO. N4008526R0178 This acquisition is being solicited on an unrestricted basis with full and open competition. THIS SOLICITATION INCLUDES CMMC LEVEL 1 (SELF) REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH DFARS 252.204-7025 (DEVIATION 2026-0038) AND 252.204-7021 (DEVIATION 2026-0038). This project is considered a �Large-scale Construction Project� as defined in FAR 22.502 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040). Accordingly, the requirements of FAR Subpart 22.5 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040) will apply. The Offeror shall submit a signed Project Labor Agreement with their Price Proposal submission, in accordance with FAR Provision 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and FAR Clause 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038). Offerors that do not include a signed Project Labor Agreement complying with the terms of FAR 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) shall be considered nonresponsive and ineligible for award. All correspondence regarding this solicitation shall be directed via email to Demetrice Jenkins at demetrice.jenkins2.civ@us.navy.mil. Description of Work: This design-bid-build project will include the construction of a multi-story steel frame 12,920 SF laboratory and office facility. The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. Construction consists of a steel frame building with a shallow foundation, metal standing seam roof and masonry and metal panel exterior walls. The project includes all pertinent site preparations and site improvements, including underground stormwater retention system, mechanical and electrical utilities, telecommunications, landscaping, drainage, parking and exterior lighting. For Option 1, P1016 Consolidated RDT&E Systems Facility, this project will include the construction of a multi-story 17,978 SF laboratory facility supported by shallow foundations. The facility will utilize structural steel framing with a standing-seam roof. Exteriors are planned as a combination of masonry veneer and metal panel siding. Demolition includes removal of Building 1272T, a 548 m2 engineering facility.

title: LOC Novel High-Density Optical Data Storage
description: 10/15/2026 AMENDMENT 0001 The purpose of this solicitation amendment is to provide Amendment 0001 and all related updated solicitation attachments, which will provide responess to all questions submitted timely to the Library of Congress by interested parties and potential offerors. All other solicitation terms and conditions remain unchanged. ************************************************************************************************************************************************** The Library of Congress, hereinafter referred to as the �Library� or �LOC�,� is exploring innovative preservation methods for its digital collections. The LOC is seeking to determine the feasibility of utilizing ultra-high density optical data storage designed for the long-term preservation of a subset of the Library�s digital collections. Currently, the Library manages over 1 billion unique objects of digital preservation data (~33 petabytes) via traditional storage methods. For longevity and reduced migration intervals, it may be reasonable for this portion of data to be permanently stored on a novel medium. The focus would be on a solution that exhibits high areal density, a long lifespan, reduced maintenance/migration cycles, is immutable, and displays a high level of durability. The Library aims to demonstrate the feasibility of an innovative optical data storage solution as a high-density, scalable, and durable medium for storing its preservation collection. The Library wishes to examine the feasibility of this method on a small subset of its digital collections. To be successful, a variety of data formats�including video, audio, text, and images� must be encoded onto the media, errors must be detected/recorded, preservation techniques must be validated and select data must be recalled/read with high fidelity. This work will contribute to the boundary pushing field of high-density optical data storage while pushing the boundaries of access and preservation. The desired outcomes of this requirement are as follows: The successful writing of 1TB of the Library�s digital data in various formats (video, audio, images, text) onto a robust high-density optical media designed to outlast legacy storage solutions at a higher areal density. The determination of the accuracy of the writing process by demonstrating early-stage error detection and ultimate 100% recovery of data. The documentation of successful processes, shortcomings, error rates, timelines, potential solutions to issues, risks, trends, and technological improvements throughout the period of performance as they pertain to the media of choice. Proof of concept for the potential indefinite storage approach of the Library�s data on a novel optical storage medium. The successful recall and reading of all Library-furnished digital files that have been encoded on the media of choice. The isolation of a subset of the data will be carefully curated and stored for the purposes of an educational and artistic display. This will used for educational and display purposes for Library visitors.
